# Adam Hickey

> Senior product designer in Minneapolis, Minnesota, for complex enterprise software: enterprise design systems, modernizing legacy products, AI-supported decision workflows and embedded senior product design. Product design for software that got complicated, plus identity and illustration made end to end. Twenty years inside enterprise platforms, design systems, and products that outgrew their original shape. Open to a senior product design role: in-house, hands-on, remote, with a team that can hire in Minnesota. Also available for select independent engagements.

Contact: adam@adamhickey.com. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamdhickey/

Every page is plain HTML with its content in the markup; nothing is rendered by script. Each page carries a canonical URL, an Open Graph card and a schema.org graph (Person, ProfessionalService, WebSite, WebPage, Article, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList), and https://adamhickey.com/sitemap.xml lists all twenty-eight pages with a last-modified date.

## How I work

Four things I bring to a product team, one page each: the situation, how it goes step by step, and the account that shows it. The same work is also on offer as an independent engagement, in one sentence at each page's close.

- [Carry the direction into something that works](https://adamhickey.com/engagement/working-product-prototype.html): a working prototype in real code, in days, engineers for leverage rather than rescue, and a build, kill or park call made on evidence.
- [Set standards other teams adopt](https://adamhickey.com/engagement/design-system-foundation.html): one design system across 40+ SAP apps, quality checks written into the release process, and teams trained until UX was their own job.
- [Own the design inside the team, not beside it](https://adamhickey.com/engagement/embedded-senior-product-design.html): learn the job before redesigning the tool, engineering in the room from the first sketch, and a change of course when users prove the first idea wrong.
- [Turn ambiguity into a decision](https://adamhickey.com/engagement/product-clarity.html): the problem in one sentence everyone recognizes, the decisions in order, one at a time, and a direction tangible enough to argue with.

## Writing

Nine articles in three collections named for what a team is hiring for: craft and code, enterprise and operational software, and AI as the material. Each answers in its first paragraph a question people ask about complicated software before they know who to ask. The index is at https://adamhickey.com/writing/index.html.

Craft and code:

- [What makes an interface feel finished?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-makes-an-interface-feel-finished.html): type on a scale, color as a measured pair, motion as a duration and a curve with a rule about interruption, a decision for every state, spacing from tokens, and the checks that hold all of it; craft as a list you can name and measure rather than a mood.
- [What does a product design engineer actually do?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-product-design-engineer-actually-do.html): the component as the deliverable, tokens that flow one way, pull requests as design reviews, prototypes on a branch, motion you can review, and the checks that hold the system; which parts of that stack a designer runs on day one.
- [What does a developer need from an interface on a bad day?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-developer-need-from-an-interface-on-a-bad-day.html): the screens a developer opens most are the ones that open when something broke, so the error message, the empty state, the log and the first ten minutes are the product; what happened, to what, why and the one thing to do next, in the five-question order developers ask, on a page dense enough to scan in a hurry.

Enterprise and operational software:

- [Designing for the moment the workflow breaks](https://adamhickey.com/writing/designing-for-the-moment-the-workflow-breaks.html): what an operational user needs when an order stalls or a transaction fails; separating what the system knows from what it assumes, and designing the recovery rather than the warning alone.
- [What does a design system need once AI is in the product?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-design-system-need-once-ai-is-in-the-product.html): six things a system built for facts needs once AI hands it claims: a slot for a value's source and age, a pending state rather than a spinner, a refusal that can never be mistaken for a suggestion, a reversible action whose pattern says what reversing means, an ink for text the system wrote, and checks that can reach the new states.
- [What I learned standardizing UX across 40+ SAP Fiori apps](https://adamhickey.com/writing/standardizing-ux-across-40-sap-fiori-apps.html): one style guide and component library, feedback loops, checks in the release process, and teams that own it; design-to-development time down by about a third, production UI defects down by roughly half.

AI as the material:

- [Enterprise AI should help people decide, not just answer](https://adamhickey.com/writing/enterprise-ai-should-help-people-decide-not-just-answer.html): the evidence beside the recommendation, calibrated rather than maximal trust, controls that have a real effect, and the decision rather than the acceptance rate as the measure.
- [What does a person need to supervise an AI agent?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-person-need-to-supervise-an-ai-agent.html): an agent is a run of decisions rather than one, so the person supervising it needs the line between what it does alone and what it asks about, drawn where a mistake gets expensive; an approval that carries its evidence; a record the run can be reconstructed from by someone who was not there; three kinds of stop, including handing a half-done queue back; an instruction they can test on last night's cases before it runs; and a measure of what they caught rather than what the agent finished.
- [What should a working prototype actually prove?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-should-a-working-prototype-actually-prove.html): whether the idea is worth building, in real code on real inputs with the people who would use it, ending in a build, kill, or park call.

## Case studies

- [One real-time view of a 450+ truck fleet](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/dispatch-complexity.html): lead product design for Midwest Couriers, a research-led dispatch cockpit.
- [Making 40+ enterprise apps feel like one product](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/sap-product-maturity.html): lead UX for a global corporation's SAP Fiori suite, under a governed design system and an accessibility standard.
- [Grant tools unified into one trusted platform](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/usda-operational-overhead.html): lead product design for the USDA-backed Nutrition Incentive Hub.
- [A global innovation network on one brand and platform](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/innovators-studio-visual-identity.html): identity and a multi-year internal platform for a worldwide innovation network.
- [13 years as an enterprise design consultant](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/enterprise-consulting.html): the RBA years, 2013 to 2026, for CBRE, Toro, Banner Bank and International Trucks.
- [8 years as a hybrid designer / developer](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/hybrid-designer.html): three Minneapolis studios, 2005 to 2013, the last five years at Pixel Farm.

## Built end to end

Products designed, built and illustrated alone.

- [How I built Door County Found](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/door-county-found.html): a curated travel guide where every place is structured data, built on Astro and edited through a web form. The guide itself is live at https://doorcountyfound.com.
- [How I built Lucy Learns](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/lucy-learns.html): a dog-training app that works offline, built for one household, with the AI tools run from a terminal instead of a chat window. The app itself is live at https://adamdhickey-collab.github.io/lucy-learns/, and the write-up embeds it at a phone's width.
- [How I built While We're Here](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/while-were-here.html): a 300mm square hardcover of essays produced from HTML and CSS through a paged-media engine.
- [How I built this site](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/this-site.html): twenty-nine pages of plain HTML with no framework and no build step, three token files under four normative specs, and nine checks that measure the rendered page before anything ships.

## Prototypes

Self-directed, interactive, on synthetic data. Design work, not client work and not shipped software.

- [An AI truck recommendation the dispatcher can check and overrule](https://adamhickey.com/prototype/dispatch-cockpit.html): human-in-the-loop AI decision support for freight dispatch, built around a hypothesis: a dispatcher spends less time reconstructing a recommendation when the interface shows what needs checking. The factors weighed with their values, where each stands and when each was last true, a close call that names its tradeoff and flags a stale figure rather than picking, outcomes on similar loads with the late ones open to inspection rather than a confidence percentage, a federal hours-of-service limit the system enforces before it scores and nothing on the screen can argue past, a one-click override of the ranking that asks why afterwards and says what it does with the answer, and the whole fleet always on screen. The interface is functional and the ranking is computed on the page; no model or dispatch system is connected. Informed by the Midwest Couriers cockpit; every figure invented, and it has not been tested with dispatchers.
